text.p: Diedrich Coffee Inc said Wednesday it expects to report a net loss of as much as $1 million in the fiscal year ended January 29, on sales of about $19 million.

The company said the loss is due to slower than anticipated sales growth in Denver and other non-core markets, disappointing holiday merchandise sales and the disruption caused by a new financial accounting system.
The company also said Steven Lupinacci has resigned as president and chief executive officer and that board member Lawrence Goelman is serving as interim president and CEO.
The anticipated loss for fiscal 1997 compares with a profit the year before of $186,000 on sales of $10.2 million.
The consensus among analysts is for a 1997 profit of $0.06 per share, according to First Call.

Diedrich said the sales increase in 1997 largely reflects an increase in the number of its coffeehouses open to 46 at the end of the latest year, from 12 the year before. But it said it underestimated the length of time it would take to build a customer base in Denver and some other non-core markets.

In addition, it said, holiday results were hurt by disappointing sales of in-store and catalog merchandise, increased temporary employment. It said the purchase of non-core inventory for the holidays proved to be unprofitable.

Finally, the company said the installation of a new accounting system resulted in management not receiving timely store-level information, although it expects it will ultimately be the source of enhanced information.
Chief Operating Officer Kerry Coin said Diedrich remains committed to expanding into new markets and believes prospects for growth are good.

"Overall, the majority of stores are cash flow-positive," Coin said in a statement. "To further bolster its financial position, the company has recently received a commitment for a $1 million line of credit on arms-length terms from a significant stockholder."
